o.text:
From Old Anatolian Turkish بینی (bäyni, “brain”), from Proto-Turkic *bẹńi (“brain”). Cognate with Turkish beyin.
Cognates
Cognate with Karakhanid [script needed] (méŋi, “brain”), Old Uyghur [script needed] (méyi, “brain”), Azerbaijani beyin (“brain”), Bashkir мейе (miyi, “brain”), Chagatai [script needed] (meyin, “brain”), Crimean Tatar miy (“brain”), Chuvash миме (mime, “brain”), Kazakh ми (mıy, “brain”), Khakas мии (mii, “brain”), Kipchak [Arabic needed] (meyi, “brain”), Kyrgyz мээ (mee, “brain”), Southern Altai мее (mee, “brain”), Tatar ми (mi, “brain”), Turkmen beýin, beýni (“brain”), Tuvan мээ (mee, “brain”), Uyghur مىڭە (mi'nge, “brain”), Uzbek miya (“brain”), Yakut мэйии (meyii, “brain”).
Borrowed from Russian шанта́ж (šantáž), from French chantage.
From Classical Persian مستقل (mustaqil), from Arabic مُسْتَقِلّ (mustaqill).
From Arabic عِبَارَة (ʕibāra). Doublet of ibarət.
Calque of Russian апте́чка (aptéčka). By surface analysis, aptek + -çə.
Borrowed from Classical Persian جَمَادِیُٱلْآخِر (jamādiyu-l-'āxir), from Arabic جُمَادَى ٱلْآخِر (jumādā l-ʔāḵir), ellipsis of شَهْر جُمَادَى ٱلْآخِر (šahr jumādā l-ʔāḵir).
